assessment: The manuscript by Mohebi et al. examines the interaction between cholinergic interneurons (CINs) and transmitter release from dopaminergic axons in the nucleus accumbens of behaving animals. The authors propose that CIN activity facilitates dopamine release through activation of DA varicosities, and enhances the motivation to obtain a reward. This study represents an important step forward in our understanding of how dopamine release regulates behavior in concert with acetylcholine signaling, and more broadly how dopamine terminals modulate behavior independently from activity at cell bodies.
